titleEn: Aiṃ is Sarasvatī. Speech, learning, a teacher's voice — all in one syllable.
meaningEn: Aiṃ is Sarasvatī's seed. Wherever a mantra wants speech, study, music or a teacher's words, this syllable is placed first. You have already heard it: oṃ aiṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ opens with it, and the Navārṇa begins aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ. The Tantras call it the vāg-bīja — the seed of the voice. It is the one great seed with no consonant at all: just the vowel ai, and the hum.
meaningHi: ऐं सरस्वती का बीज है। जहाँ मंत्र में बोली, पढ़ाई, संगीत या गुरु की सीख माँगी जाती है, वहाँ यह अक्षर सबसे पहले रखा जाता है। आपने इसे सुना है: ॐ ऐं सरस्वत्यै नमः इसी से शुरू होता है, और नवार्ण मंत्र ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं से। तंत्र इसे वाग्-बीज कहते हैं — वाणी का बीज। बड़े बीजों में यही अकेला है जिसमें कोई व्यंजन नहीं: बस स्वर ऐ, और गूँज।
sayItLike: eye-m — 'eye', then close the lips into a hum

words.glossEn: the vowel — read by the Tantras as Sarasvatī herself
words.glossHi: स्वर — तंत्र इसे सरस्वती ही पढ़ते हैं
words.grammar: no consonant: this seed is a bare vowel — Vāgīśvarī, the Lady of Speech, in the Śāradā-tilaka

words.glossEn: the dot (ं) — the closing hum, bindu and nāda
words.glossHi: बिंदी (ं) — अंत की गूँज, बिन्दु और नाद
words.grammar: the Varada Tantra's kośa reads the dot as 'what takes sorrow away' — tradition's attribution, not a meaning

source.text: Śāradā-tilaka Tantra (11th c.), Sarasvatī / Vāgīśvarī paṭala; Varada Tantra as quoted in Woodroffe, Garland of Letters (1922)
source.ref: the vāg-bīja; first seed of the Navārṇa, where the Saptaśatī vidhi names it 'aiṃ bījam'
source.note: A seed has no dictionary meaning. 'Aiṃ is Sarasvatī' is the Tantras' assignment, held for a thousand years; the letter-by-letter reading is their kośa method, not etymology.

significance.textSays: The Śāradā-tilaka gives aiṃ to Vāgīśvarī, the Lady of Speech; the Saptaśatī vidhi names it the bīja of the Navārṇa; the Varada Tantra's kośa reads ai as Sarasvatī and the closing dot as 'that which takes sorrow away'.
significance.traditionSays: The seed in Sarasvatī's own mantra; first of the Navārṇa's three seeds; first of the Bālā triad aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ; read by modern teachers as Mahāsarasvatī within the Navārṇa.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That it improves memory, speech or examinations. It names Sarasvatī by sound; asking is the devotee's, granting is hers.
